name: Cà Phê Sữa Đá
description: Vietnamese iced coffee: strong, dark coffee slow-dripped through a phin onto condensed milk, then poured over ice.

steps.text: Spoon the condensed milk into a heatproof glass and set the phin on top.
Add the coffee to the phin, shake it level, and press the insert on lightly.
Pour in about 20 ml of boiling water to bloom.
Fill the phin with the rest of the water, cover, and let it drip slowly, about 4–5 minutes.
Stir the coffee into the condensed milk, then pour it over a glass full of ice.

tips: Dripping too fast? Press the insert a little tighter next time. Too slow? Loosen it.

sources.name: Nguyen Coffee Supply — Cà phê sữa đá
The Woks of Life — Vietnamese coffee

name: Cà Phê Trứng (Egg Coffee)
description: Hanoi's dessert-like coffee: strong phin coffee under a thick, custardy foam of whipped yolk and condensed milk.

steps.text: Set a small cup in a bowl of hot water to keep it warm, then brew a short, strong coffee into it with the phin (or pull an espresso).
Meanwhile, whisk the egg yolk, condensed milk and sugar until pale, thick and doubled in volume. That's 3–5 minutes with a hand mixer.
Spoon the egg foam gently over the hot coffee.
Dust with cocoa and eat the top with a spoon before stirring the rest.

tips: Created in 1946 by Nguyễn Văn Giảng at Hanoi's Metropole Hotel, when milk was scarce.

name: Cà Phê Cốt Dừa (Coconut Coffee)
description: A Hanoi café favourite: a coconut-condensed-milk slushy with strong coffee poured over the top.

steps.text: Brew a strong coffee with the phin (or use a double espresso) and let it cool a little.
Blend the coconut cream, condensed milk and ice on high until it's smooth and slushy.
Spoon the slush into a glass and pour the coffee over the top.

name: Turkish Coffee
description: Powder-fine coffee simmered in a cezve with sugar, served unfiltered under a velvety foam.

steps.text: Put the cold water, coffee and sugar in the cezve. Sugar goes in now, never after.
Stir just enough to combine, then leave the spoon out.
Warm over low heat. When foam rises toward the rim, lift it off the heat before it boils over.
Spoon some foam into the cup, return the cezve to the heat and let it rise once more.
Pour slowly into the cup and let the grounds settle for a minute before sipping.

tips: Serve with a glass of water and something sweet, like Turkish delight.

name: Café de Olla
description: Mexican pot coffee simmered with cinnamon and piloncillo. Warm, spiced and lightly caramel-sweet.

steps.text: Put the water, piloncillo, cinnamon and any other spices in a pot (a clay olla if you have one).
Bring to a boil, stirring until the piloncillo has dissolved.
Take it off the heat, stir in the coffee, cover and steep.
Strain through a fine sieve or cloth into mugs.

tips: Traditionally served black, no milk. Steep 8 minutes for extra strength.

sources.name: Mexico in My Kitchen — Café de olla

name: Café Bombón
description: Espresso layered over sweetened condensed milk in a small glass. Stir when you're ready.

steps.text: Pour the condensed milk into a small clear glass.
Pull a double espresso and pour it gently over the back of a spoon so it sits on top.
Serve layered and stir just before drinking.

name: Café Cubano
description: Moka-pot coffee whipped with sugar into a sweet 'espumita' foam. Served in tiny cups.

steps.text: Fill the moka pot base with water and the basket with coffee, level but not tamped. Set it on medium-high heat.
Put the sugar in a small metal jug or cup.
As soon as the first few drops of coffee appear, pour about a teaspoon of them onto the sugar.
Beat the sugar and coffee hard with a spoon into a thick, pale paste. This is the espumita.
When the pot finishes, pour the coffee slowly into the paste, stirring gently. A foam will rise to the top.
Serve in small cups with a layer of foam on each.

sources.name: Home Espresso Lab — Cafecito with espumita

name: Swedish Egg Coffee
description: A Scandinavian-American trick: mixing a raw egg into the grounds before boiling gives a remarkably smooth, clear cup.

steps.text: Mix the coffee grounds with the egg (and crushed shell, if you're going traditional) into a damp paste.
Bring the water to a boil, then stir in the paste.
Simmer for about 3 minutes. The egg will clump with the grounds.
Take it off the heat and add about 60 ml of cold water to settle everything.
Strain through a fine sieve and serve.

tips: The egg is fully cooked by the boil, and it takes the bitterness with it.

sources.name: America's Test Kitchen — What is Swedish egg coffee?

name: Qahwa (Arabic Coffee)
description: Lightly roasted coffee simmered with cardamom, and sometimes saffron. Golden, fragrant, and served with dates.

steps.text: Bring the water to a boil in a dallah or saucepan.
Stir in the coffee, lower the heat and simmer.
Add the crushed cardamom (and cloves, or a few saffron threads) and simmer a few minutes more.
Let the grounds settle for a minute, then pour through a strainer into small handleless cups.

tips: Traditionally unsweetened and served alongside dates.

name: Café con Leche
description: Strong coffee and scalded milk in equal parts. The everyday breakfast coffee of Spain and Latin America.

steps.text: Brew strong coffee in a moka pot, or pull a double espresso.
Heat the milk in a small pan until tiny bubbles form at the edge. Take it off before it boils.
Pour the coffee and milk into a mug in roughly equal amounts, and sweeten to taste.

sources.name: Mashed — Café con leche vs café au lait

name: Einspänner (Vienna Coffee)
description: A Viennese café classic: strong black coffee under a thick cap of lightly sweetened whipped cream.

steps.text: Whip the cream and sugar to soft-to-medium peaks.
Pull a double espresso into a small glass, adding a splash of hot water if you like.
Pile the cream on top. Don't stir; sip the coffee through the cream.
Dust with cocoa if you like.

tips: Iced version: pour espresso over ice and a splash of milk, then top with the cream.

name: Butter Coffee
description: Hot coffee blended with butter (and often MCT oil) into a rich, frothy, latte-like cup.

steps.text: Brew a mug of coffee however you like.
Add the hot coffee and butter (plus 1 tsp–1 tbsp MCT or coconut oil, if you have it) to a blender.
Blend for about 20–30 seconds until frothy and creamy, then pour into a mug.

tips: A handheld milk frother in a tall jar works too. Leave room for it to expand.

name: Mazagran
description: The 'original iced coffee': sweetened coffee with lemon juice over ice. Think coffee lemonade.

steps.text: Brew a double espresso or strong moka pot coffee and stir in the sugar while it's hot.
Let it cool to room temperature.
Stir in the lemon juice.
Pour over a tall glass of ice and garnish with a lemon slice and mint.
